name: Boaz
overview: Boaz was a male member of the tribe of Judah, known primarily as the kinsman of Naomi's deceased husband who redeemed Ruth. He was a prominent figure in Bethlehem and played a crucial role in the redemption of Ruth, a Moabitess, demonstrating faithfulness to covenantal duties within Israel.
namesAndTitles: The name Boaz, likely meaning 'in him is strength,' reflects qualities of reliability and power. This proper name, as noted in Ruth 2:1, was not given by God but carries significance in illustrating his character and role.
familyAndRelationships: Boaz was husband to Ruth and father of Obed, as inferred from Ruth 4:10, 4:13. He was also the son of Salmon, explicitly stated in Ruth 4:21. These relationships connect him directly to the Messianic lineage.
scriptureSignificance: Boaz exemplifies the biblical role of the kinsman-redeemer, faithfully fulfilling the responsibility to redeem a relative, which prefigures Christ's redemptive work for His people. His marriage to Ruth, a Gentile, highlights God's sovereign plan to include all nations in the Messianic line. Through his son Obed, Boaz is an ancestor of King David, anchoring him in the lineage of the Messiah.
